extracted.intended_audience: economists, policy analysts, researchers and policymakers interested in Quebec and Canadian interprovincial and international trade (provincial-level economic analysts)
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretation and quantitative analysis of Quebec's interprovincial and international trade flows (1974–1989) using input-output reestimations, sectoral balances, coverage ratios, and sensitivity checks. The page explains metrics, caveats, and methods for comparing periods, regions and product groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taux d'approvisionnement (supply rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Le ratio d'approvisionnement mesure jusqu'á quel point le marché provincial est approvisionné par les manufacturiers locaux plutôt que par les autres manufacturiers canadiens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess how much a provincial market is supplied by local manufacturers versus elsewhere in Canada; contrasted with the ratio d'expéditions locales. Use region- and sector-level data (tables cited) to compute and track changes over time (e.g., increases in Atlantic self-supply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratio d'expéditions locales (local shipments ratio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Le ratio d'expéditions locales (ou rapport au marché local) indique dans quelle mesure les manufacturiers d'une province dépendent du marché provincial plutôt que du reste du Canada pour leurs ventes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complementary to taux d'approvisionnement: one measures market supply, the other measures manufacturer dependence on local market. Compare across periods/regions to infer shifts in market orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moyennes des diagonales du tableau d'échanges interprovinciaux (diagonal averages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prendre les moyennes de chacune des diagonales du tableau (les diagonales proches de la diagonale centrale représentent le taux d'auto-approvisionnement; les diagonales plus éloignées représentent les taux d'approvisionnement interprovinciaux).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This simple mathematical exercise is proposed as an indicator of the importance of geographic proximity for trade flows. The text explicitly warns this is 'un indice (non rigoureux sur le plan statistique)'. Useful for qualitative inference about proximity effects and their evolution over time (e.g., 1974→1984).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance des expéditions interprovinciales (interprovincial shipment balance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyse des soldes (excédents/déficits) des expéditions entre les régions canadiennes durant une période donnée, ventilée par secteur (manufacturier, primaire, secondaire, tertiaire) et par marché (reste du Canada vs étranger).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute sectoral surpluses/deficits (in $) and express as percent of total shipments where relevant. Use balances to identify surplus sectors (e.g., habillement, papiers) and deficit sectors (e.g., aliments, machinerie). Compare across years and markets to detect structural shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traitement et interprétation des données confidentielles / données manquantes
rubrics_metrics.description: Les chiffres d'expéditions peuvent être confidentiels (données non publiées) pour certains sous-secteurs (ex. boissons), empêchant des comparaisons directes entre périodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report exemplifies an approximation practice: when data for a sub-sector are suppressed, one may approximate deficits by assuming the suppressed shipments are zero (hypothèse extrême) to obtain a broad bound, but the text cautions about the limits of such approximations and invites careful interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prudence face aux changements de classification (classification changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Des changements de classification interviennent dans les compilations de Statistique Canada, rendant parfois impossibles des comparaisons directes de l'ampleur des déficits entre périodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing sectoral balances across years, account explicitly for classification breaks; consult annexes and methodology notes before drawing conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taux de couverture (coverage rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mesure présentant la capacité d'une région à 'couvrir' ses importations par ses exportations; the text uses both conventional coverage notions and a specific ratio shown in parentheses: X/(X+M+production intérieure) where X=exportations, M=importations, plus domestic production for final domestic consumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the annex figures (e.g., fig. III.3, III.15) for coverage rates by region and by sector. Be explicit which numerator/denominator definition is used (exports/imports or exports/(exports+imports+domestic production)) because interpretation differs markedly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilisation des tableaux input–output provinciaux réestimés (balancing of IO tables)
rubrics_metrics.description: Les données utilisées proviennent des tableaux input–output provinciaux de Statistique Canada, réestimés pour satisfaire un ensemble de contraintes nationales et régionales (processus d'équilibrage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These reestimations permit estimating flows beyond mere expéditions manufacturières (incluant primaire, secondaire, tertiaire). The report references Durand (1989) for the balancing process; analysts should be aware that numbers are adjusted to meet constraints and check annex methodological notes for implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions et analyses de sensibilité (exclude specific product categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstraction faite de certaines catégories (céréales, produits agricoles, pétrole, charbon et combustibles minéraux) pour observer l'effet sur parts régionales et soldes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recompute shares and balances excluding dominant commodity groups to reveal underlying diversification (e.g., Prairies' share falls drastically when petroleum/cereals are excluded). Use as a sensitivity check to detect dependence on a few sectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degré d'ouverture (openness degree relative to GDP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mesure de l'ouverture de l'économie: exportations (et importations) rapportées au PIB (ex. exportations totales = 54.5% du PIB québécois en 1984 vs 59.4% pour le Canada).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to compare regional openness and as a condition for welfare improvement. The text treats lower openness as a challenge for economic policy and market diversification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapport produits primaires / produits secondaires (primary/secondary ratio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ratio des exportations (ou importations) du secteur primaire sur celles du secteur secondaire pour évaluer la composition sectorielle des échanges (e.g., Quebec primary/secondary exports declined from 9.6% in 1984 to 5.5% in 1989).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track trends by market (rest of Canada, U.S., Europe) to see structural shifts: falling ratios indicate growing predominance of manufactured (secondary) exports. Use international breakdowns to assess market-specific composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ajustements pour effets de transit et différences BSQ vs Statistique Canada
rubrics_metrics.description: Données du Bureau de la Statistique du Québec (BSQ) peuvent différer des estimations de Statistique Canada en raison d'ajustements pour le transit (production intérieure exportée via le Québec, importations québécoises expédiées ailleurs au Canada, réexpédition d'importations d'autres provinces au Québec).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysts should consult the annex comment on BSQ methods and the magnitude of adjustments. Recognize that differing accounting of transit flows changes provincial trade tallies and cross-source comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classements et mesures par habitant (per-capita export rankings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilisation de mesures par habitant pour comparer performances (ex. Moreau's estimate that Quebec ranked seventh worldwide in manufacturing exports per capita).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per-capita export rankings are useful for international benchmarking but must be interpreted with care (population size, sector composition). Cross-check sources and years for consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyse temporelle par périodes (time-period trend comparisons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparaisons structurées entre sub-périodes (e.g., 1967–1974, 1974–1979, 1979–1984, 1984–1989) to identify trends in shares, balances, and sectoral composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent series and be mindful of classification changes, confidential data, and reestimation adjustments when making period-to-period comparisons. Trends reported include declines/increases in provincial shares and sectoral shifts (e.g., Quebec's share of interprovincial exports falling from 28.2% to 23.5% between 1974 and 1984).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ventilation marché par marché (market-by-market sectoral breakdown)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disaggregation of balances and flows by destination/market (Ontario, rest of Canada, United States, Europe, Japan, Southeast Asia) and by sector/product (e.g., clothing, papers, machinery, automobiles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify dominant markets (U.S. receives >77% of Quebec exports in 1987) and problem sectors (automobile deficit for Quebec). Combine market and product breakdowns to target diversification strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat emptor / vérification de la robustesse (data quality caveats and robustness checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated cautions to the reader about data limitations, confidentiality, classification changes and the need to consult annexes (annexe 1 on quality and robustness; annexe 2 with tables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before drawing policy conclusions, perform robustness checks, consult annex methodology, and when possible use calibrated/balanced data (the report promises to return to subject with calibrated data in a later section).
